prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, specifically: execution and properties of operations with exponential numbers and logarithms, solving first and second-degree equations, systems of equations
Some basic knowledge of physics, specifically: kinetic and potential energy, work, Coulomb's law, electric charge, electric dipole, electric current

learning_outcomes.text: Provide basic knowledge of materials chemistry aimed at understanding the structure and properties of different classes of materials.
Acquire basic knowledge of the main classes of materials, their properties, and applications.
Be able to understand the principles underlying the design, development, and realization of latest-generation products of interest in the dental field.
Practical application of knowledge acquired during the course.
Be in possession of basic chemical notions on the composition, structure, properties, and transformations of matter.
Be in possession of fundamental knowledge on atomic structure, the nature of chemical bonding, and the structure of molecules.
Be in possession of notions on the properties of the gaseous state and solutions.
Know how to balance a chemical equation and determine quantitative relationships in a reaction.
Be in possession of useful knowledge to evaluate the concentration and dilution of aqueous solutions.
Be able to represent the formula and predictable molecular geometry of simple binary, ternary, and coordination compounds.
Know how to interpret the behavior of a system under chemical equilibrium conditions in the gaseous phase and in aqueous solution, also at a quantitative level.
Be in possession of in-depth knowledge to evaluate the degree of acidity (pH) of aqueous solutions and the conditions for the precipitation of sparingly soluble compounds in solution.
Know the basic concepts of chemical kinetics.
Know the energetics of chemical transformations (chemical thermodynamics) and can evaluate the spontaneity of a reaction.
Be able to apply theoretically learned concepts to real cases.
Have developed the ability to perform exact and approximate calculations by applying the laws of chemistry and stoichiometry to concrete cases (numerical exercises and laboratory activities).
Be able to solve, with scientific and logical reasoning, stoichiometry problems using their chemical and mathematical knowledge.
Be able to interpret experimental facts in light of chemical theory (atomic structure, bonding, equilibria etc).
Be able to communicate and explain, using correct chemical terms, all the contents of the course.
Be able, with the acquired knowledge, to follow and understand the lessons of subsequent, more specialized courses.
Be able to understand the principles underlying the design, development, and realization of latest-generation products.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: States of aggregation of matter. Homogeneous and heterogeneous systems. Substances and chemical elements.
Atomic structure of matter: Atomic theory. Properties of the atom. Nuclear structure and isotopes. Atomic weights. Chemical symbols and their quantitative meaning.
Nomenclature of main chemical substances: Molecular and ionic chemical substances, chemical formulas of simple compounds.
Chemical reactions: Writing and balancing chemical reactions. Calculations with chemical formulas and equations: Avogadro's number, concept of mole. Determination of chemical formulas. Stoichiometry.
The gaseous state: Gaseous pressure and its measurement. Ideal gas law. Gas mixtures and partial pressures. Basics of the kinetic theory of gases.
Thermochemistry: Energy and units of measurement. Heat of reaction. Enthalpy and enthalpy change. Thermochemical equations.

Atomic structure: Quantum numbers and atomic orbitals. Electron spin and Pauli exclusion principle. Aufbau principle. Configuration of atoms. Hund's rule. The periodic system of elements. Periodic properties of elements: ionization potential, electron affinity.

Chemical bonding: Ionic bond. Covalent bond: generalities, octet rule. Lewis formulas. Delocalized bonds and resonance. Bond distance, order, and energy. Molecular geometry and dipole moment. Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory. Valence bond theory: hybrid orbitals, resonance, multiple bonds. Magnetic properties of molecules. Molecular orbital theory.
States of matter.
Chemical kinetics: Reaction rate. Catalysis.
Reactions and chemical equilibria: Equilibrium state. Chemical equilibrium. Equilibrium constant. Heterogeneous equilibria. Shift of equilibrium: Le Chatelier's principle.

Acid-base equilibria: Definitions of acids and bases according to Arrhenius, Brønsted-Lowry, and Lewis. Molecular structure and strength of acids. Ionization of water. Solution of a strong acid or base. The pH of a solution. Ionization equilibria of a weak acid or base. Hydrolysis. Buffer solutions.
Solubility equilibria: Solubility product. Common ion effect. Precipitation criteria. Effect of pH on solubility.

Thermodynamics and equilibrium: First law of thermodynamics. Entropy and second law of thermodynamics. Standard entropies and third law of thermodynamics. Free energy and spontaneity. Relationship between free energy and equilibrium constants.
Brief introduction to computational methods in Chemistry.
Computer exercises.
Brief introduction to chemical laboratory practice.
Laboratory exercises.
Changes of state: Phase transitions. Phase equilibria. State diagrams.
The liquid state: Main properties of liquids.
The solid state: Crystalline structures. Molecular, covalent, ionic solids. Metallic solids.
Introduction to the chemistry of organic compounds.

Hydrocarbons: general classification. Saturated, unsaturated, and aromatic hydrocarbons, nomenclature, graphical representation. Constitutional isomerism. Stereochemistry. Chirality, plane, and center of symmetry. Chiral molecules.
Main functional groups.
Chemistry of elements of interest in dental materials.
Introduction to materials science and technology.
Crystalline and amorphous structure of materials. Solidification and crystalline imperfections.
Thermally activated processes and diffusion in solids.
State diagrams and metallic alloys (binary state diagrams). Metallic materials and metallic alloys.
Polymeric materials. Ceramic materials. Composite materials.
Nanostructured materials.
Corrosion and protection of materials.
Electrical and thermal properties of materials.
Biological materials and biomaterials. Materials of interest in dental technology.

assessment_methods.method: Exercises completed during the course (Laboratory module)

assessment_rules: To be admitted to the oral exam for the General Chemistry and Materials Chemistry modules, a minimum score of 18/30 on the respective written exam is required. The final grade, expressed out of thirty, will consider both the written and oral exam evaluations. For the Laboratory module, assessment is based on exercises completed during the course.
